key_insight: AI detection of pulmonary TB on chest X-rays approached WHO triage targets, with pooled sensitivity of 89.6% and specificity of 68.9%, but neither target was clearly met.
clinical_relevance: AI could support TB screening and triage where radiologists are scarce, but accuracy varies across products and settings.
method: Systematic review of five databases covering January 2020–March 2026.
Bivariate random-effects meta-analysis of nine evaluations from three independent clinical cohorts.
Risk of bias assessed with QUADAS-2 and evidence certainty with GRADE.
evidence_signal: Among 21 included studies, only one was prospective, fully verified, externally validated and met both WHO triage thresholds; certainty was low for sensitivity and very low for specificity.
watch_item: The review missed additional eligible clinical evaluations, and pooling across only three cohorts limits confidence in generalizability.
paper_title: Artificial intelligence for pulmonary tuberculosis detection on chest X-ray images: A systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis
